title: Business Organization & Environment Adventure 1: Sectors & Stakeholders
welcome_lead: Today you'll map the four sectors of business and the internal & external stakeholders who care about them.
meta_desc: Business Management: primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary sectors plus internal and external stakeholders.
final_note: You learned the four sectors of activity and distinguished internal from external stakeholders.

concepts.def: Inside the firm: owners, managers, employees
Outside the firm: customers, suppliers, govt

walkthroughs.body_html:
Economies are split into four productive sectors.

Primary extracts raw materials — mining, fishing, agriculture.

Secondary processes them — car plants, breweries, textiles.

Tertiary delivers services — banks, hotels, hospitals.

Quaternary sells knowledge — R&D labs, software houses, consultancies.

As economies develop, employment shifts from primary toward tertiary and quaternary — a pattern known as sectoral change.

A stakeholder is any group affected by a firm's actions.

Internal: owners/shareholders, managers, employees — inside the organisation.

External: customers, suppliers, creditors, government, local community, pressure groups, competitors.

Their interests often conflict: shareholders want dividends, employees want higher wages, customers want lower prices.

A supermarket cutting supplier prices pleases shareholders (higher margins) but harms suppliers (lower revenue).

Building a new factory creates jobs (community) but raises pollution (pressure groups).

Managers must balance these interests — the basis of CSR and stakeholder theory (Freeman, 1984).

mcqs.q: Which sector includes software development and R&D consultancies?
Which of these is an INTERNAL stakeholder?
Are all organisations in the private sector profit-driven?
options: The private sector means businesses that keep their accounts secret.
Stakeholder conflicts are settled by public referendum.
No — the private sector also includes non-profit social enterprises, charities and cooperatives that trade to pursue social aims rather than shareholder profit.

mcqs.q: Can a business belong to more than one sector of the economy?
options: Stakeholder conflicts are settled by public referendum.
Every business fits into exactly one sector.
Yes — vertically integrated firms can grow raw materials, process them and run shops, operating across primary, secondary and tertiary sectors at once.
Sectors are assigned to businesses by lottery each year.

mcqs.q: Do stakeholder conflicts mean a business is being run badly?
options: Sectors are assigned to businesses by lottery each year.
In a well-managed business all stakeholders want the same thing.
No — conflicts, such as shareholders wanting dividends while employees want pay rises, are normal because interests differ; management's job is to balance them.
Stakeholder conflicts are settled by public referendum.
